source_pdf_note: THE FIRST SECTION IN THIS REGISTRY THAT IS NOT THE KITCHEN SYSTEM. Until 2026-08-27 Registry.lookup built source_ref from _manifest.json's single source_pdf, so a code held here would have cited the wrong book. source_pdf is now a per-section fact and the manifest's value is only the default. Volume named because docs/Cesar_Volumes_Index.md requires it: a code absent from the book you have is not a code absent from the book.
source_pages: printed p.214-220 / PDF 216-222, all seven read from 150-dpi renders 2026-08-27
family_note: A family in this registry has meant a CABINET height - H.78, Wall H.48. This one is not a height at all: a sheet has no height until somebody orders one. The key is kept because the loader requires it and because these codes genuinely share their grammar, their minimum and their surcharges; it is named for the book and the chapter rather than for a dimension, and nothing should read a number out of it.
extraction_note: Demand-driven, 2026-08-27: the island of 545 Avenida Primavera is clad across its back with two panels 1200 wide and 880 tall, and no article in the Kitchen System prices a panel at 880 - that chapter is priced by CABINET height and stops at 84 in two of the three collections. Account: claude/findings-2026-08-27-vol3-panels-read.md.
pricing_note: points_per_m2 is a rate, not a price. Contract v2 1.2 keeps points out of the object; they live here because the order needs them and the drawing must not.
companions_note: p.214 prices two things that ride with a panel and neither is a panel: the fixing kit, PER BASE UNIT WIDTH, and the adjustable foot, each. They are held in _manifest.json under hardware.linear_element_panel_fixings because the kit's quantity comes from the RUN and not from this article - four 600 units behind two 1200 panels take four kits - and companion_refs has no way to say that today.

panel_melamine_12.description: Panel in melamine on 2 sides, 1,2 cm thick with ABS edge
panel_melamine_12.handed_note: A sheet has no hand. It is cut from a board and has no hinge, no 45-degree edge and no end it belongs at - which is exactly what separates it from the adjoining end side panel of Volume 2.
panel_melamine_12.minimum_note: Printed at the head of every one of the six pages: 'Minimum invoicing quantity: 0.5 m2.' A panel smaller than that is invoiced AT 0,5 m2 - the surface is the order line, not the piece.
panel_melamine_12.max_sheet_note: The only dimensional fact the page states, drawn beside the block as 205 x 278 cm. It is the SHEET, not the article: the article has no width and no height, and both come from the order.
panel_melamine_12.mounting_note: printed p.214, in the catalog's own words: 'If it is used as a floor-standing panel behind a base unit or as a floor-standing end side panel, 0.5-cm high feet will be mounted that must be calculated separately.' The foot is 990408 and is a separate order line; its design height is 0 with 5 mm of travel - see claude/repo-state.md, 'The 5 mm foot'.

front_layout.note: A PANEL HAS NO FRONT. Stated rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs defaults a missing layout to 'single' and would hang a door leaf on a flat board.

panel_melamine_12.not_buildable_reason: The registry holds it and the picker will offer it; the generator cannot draw it yet. A sheet is not an end panel turned sideways: an end panel carries its thickness on x and its front edge in the plane of the doors, and a panel behind a run carries its thickness on y and no front edge at all. Until Generator has that orientation and a placement against the BACK of a selected run, drawing one would put a board in the wrong plane and call it an order. Geometry is the next commit.
panel_melamine_12.thickness_note: Thickness is the article's ONLY fixed dimension and it is carried in depth_mm, because that is the axis a sheet is thin on: a board standing across the back of a run is wide on x, tall on z and thin on y. The Volume 2 end panel puts its 22 on width_mm instead, and the two must not be read the same way.

surcharges.note: Identical on all six pages of the chapter, each per piece.

panel_melamine_12.notes: Finishes printed beside the block: Bianco, Canapa, Grigio fumo.

AND THE POINTS ARE NOT MONOTONE: C at 2,2 costs 339 against B's 405, and D's 1,8 and 2,2 are both 670. Recorded as printed.
